subtitle: Lesson 20 · Working With GPUs in PyTorch

eyebrow: autocast picks precision per op, not globally
code:
with torch.autocast(device_type="cuda", dtype=torch.float16):
    outputs = model(inputs)
    loss = loss_fn(outputs, labels)

loss.backward()
optimizer.step()
caption: GEMM-heavy, compute-bound layers get the real Tensor Core speedup

eyebrow: GradScaler prevents float16 gradients from vanishing
code:
scaler = torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler()

scaler.scale(loss).backward()   # scale up first
scaler.step(optimizer)          # unscale, then step
scaler.update()                 # adjust scale for next time
caption: Small gradients would otherwise underflow to exactly zero in float16
